note: Examples by what they DO. `needs` says what has to be on disk: `compiler` is an npm install away, `repo` means a Ranger checkout because the gallery is there.

examples.title: Hello, and the build loop
examples.does: One class, one print — and the `rgr` loop that fails loudly when the compile fails.

examples.title: A parser and evaluator, in four languages
examples.does: Tokenises and evaluates arithmetic with a recursive-descent parser, then runs the SAME source as JavaScript, Python and Go.
examples.run: rgr run Calc.rgr && rgr run Calc.rgr -l=python && rgr run Calc.rgr -l=go

examples.title: A PDF with no browser in it
examples.does: Lays a document out with EVG — a CSS engine written in Ranger — and prints it as a real PDF with embedded fonts and vector graphics.

examples.title: A Figma file, written and read
examples.does: Reads a .fig (Kiwi + zstd) and writes one: frames, text, vector networks, a thumbnail. Round-trips a running app's screens into a design file.

examples.title: Editing a document the way an agent should
examples.does: Reads a document's outline, measures it, patches it with invertible operations and undoes the patch — the surface this plugin's `evg-edit` skill drives.

examples.title: An application, not a picture of one
examples.does: A routed, responsive, accessible app written as HTML-shaped markup and checked without a browser.

examples.title: The same screen on iOS and Android
examples.does: One Ranger source driving a Swift host and a Kotlin host — the layout, the state machine and the list are shared; only the window is native.
teaches: a native host around shared logic

examples.title: More than one module
examples.does: `ranger.json`, dependencies by path, and a build that resolves them — for when files and `Import` stop being enough. It sits beside the compiler rather than in the gallery: packaging is the language's, not an application's.
